name: Business Current Account Opening — Non-Functional Requirements
description: Per-phase NFRs for JRN-004. Defines latency targets, throughput, availability targets, security classification, data classification, and regulatory SLAs. NFRs reflect the operational reality of a UK mid-tier commercial bank's business banking division, the Important Business Service obligations under PRA SS1/21 / FCA PS21/3, and the specific regulatory SLAs imposed by MLR 2017 Regulations 28 and 33, OFSI sanctions obligations, and Companies House API dependency targets. Business account opening has materially different volume and latency characteristics from personal account opening (JRN-001) — volumes are lower but individual application complexity (UBO identification, multiple individual verifications, EDD path) is significantly higher.

baseline_assumptions.peak_hour_volume: A mid-tier UK commercial bank processing c. 50 business account applications per hour at peak. Sustained throughput: 20 applications/hour average; 80 applications/hour peak for a major campaign. Business account applications are a lower-volume, higher-complexity workflow than personal account opening.
baseline_assumptions.important_business_service: Business Account Opening is classified as an Important Business Service (IBS) under PRA SS1/21. Assumed impact tolerance: maximum 8 hours cumulative downtime in any 12-month rolling period for the full business account opening journey (less time-critical than personal account opening due to multi-day SLA, but still an IBS).
baseline_assumptions.data_residency: All personal data (PII) and company data must remain within the UK. No PII traversal through non-UK CDN nodes or cloud regions.
baseline_assumptions.companies_house_api_dependency: Companies House API (api.company-information.service.gov.uk) is an external government-operated API with an SLA of approximately 99.9% monthly availability (historically). The journey design accommodates temporary CH API unavailability via asynchronous retry — application is not blocked if CH API is temporarily down, it is held and retried automatically.
baseline_assumptions.regulatory_reporting_reference: NFR SLAs for sanctions screening and OFSI notification are hard regulatory obligations. UBO identification completeness is a regulatory obligation under MLR 2017 — there is no performance target for completeness; it must be 100%.

latency.notes: Form rendering and submission via SVC-017 (Digital Channels). Business application forms are more complex than personal (additional fields: company name, CH number, SIC codes, entity type) — slight latency uplift from JRN-001. Eligibility check (entity type, deduplication) must return within 1,000ms at p95.

throughput.burst_handling: Horizontal auto-scaling of SVC-017. Queue-backed processing for eligibility checks.
throughput.notes: Much lower volume than personal account opening. Auto-scaling requirements are correspondingly lower but the same architecture applies.

availability.degraded_mode: If SVC-017 is degraded, static form capture with async submission. Eligibility check deferred to BPH-002.

nfr.security_notes: No authentication at initiation. Device fingerprinting and fraud signals captured passively. CAPTCHA on bot-detection.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — UK GDPR personal data for the applicant; Companies House data is public record but treated as business-sensitive in context.
data_classification.retention: Application data retained for 5 years post-application per MLR 2017 Regulation 40. Abandoned applications purged after 72 hours (business applications allowed 48-hour additional grace vs personal).

regulatory_sla.obligation: No specific regulatory SLA for this phase. BBRS disclosure must be present on eligibility screen for eligible SME customers (GOV-002-R03).

latency.notes: Companies House API is an external government API. Normal response times are sub-second but the API has documented latency spikes and occasional degradation. p95 of 3,000ms accommodates normal CH API variability. p99 of 8,000ms is the threshold for triggering async retry path. Customers should not experience > 8 seconds of visible wait — if CH API is slow, the verification is moved to async background processing and PER-002 is notified when complete.

throughput.burst_handling: CH API calls are made per application — no batching. Companies House rate limits apply (600 requests per 5 minutes per API key). API key rotation policy required if volume approaches rate limit.
throughput.notes: At peak 80 applications/hour, the CH API call rate is well below the published rate limit. Monitor for burst patterns.

availability.degraded_mode: If Companies House API is unavailable, application is held in queue. Automatic retry every 15 minutes for up to 4 hours. If CH API remains unavailable for >4 hours, PER-002 is notified of delay. RM can manually progress high-priority applications with offline CH verification using the Companies House web portal as fallback.
availability.planned_maintenance_window: Companies House API has its own maintenance windows — bank system should tolerate these via async retry. BCOBS advance notice not required for external API dependency degradation.

nfr.security_notes: CH API is called server-side by SVC-005 using an API key stored in secrets management. API key is rotated quarterly. No customer-provided data is sent to Companies House beyond the company registration number (a public identifier).

data_classification.sensitivity: MEDIUM — Companies House data is public record, but the bank's processing of it in combination with application data is business-sensitive. PSC data relating to natural persons is personal data under UK GDPR.
data_classification.retention: Companies House verification results retained for 5 years per MLR 2017 Regulation 40.

regulatory_sla.obligation: MLR 2017 Regulation 28(11): company identity must be verified from a reliable independent source before the business relationship is established. Companies House verification is the primary mechanism for this obligation. No specific time limit is imposed but CDD must be complete before account opening.

companies_house_api_targets.notes: These targets are based on observed Companies House API performance. Monitoring alerts should fire when p95 latency exceeds 3,000ms or error rate exceeds 1% over a 5-minute window.

latency.notes: UBO identification is primarily UI-driven (applicant confirms director/UBO list). Server-side processing builds DirectorRecord and UBO entities from the CH API data — low computational cost. Latency here is dominated by form rendering and applicant interaction time, not system processing.

throughput.notes: Entity creation for DirectorRecord and UBO is per application, with multiple records per application (average 2–4 directors, 1–3 UBOs). System must handle bulk entity creation efficiently.

availability.degraded_mode: UBO identification data can be cached from the BPH-002 CH API response — if SVC-005 is partially degraded, the UI can still render and capture the UBO list; entity creation is queued for when the service recovers.

nfr.security_notes: Applicant must be authenticated to submit UBO identification. UBO personal data (name, DOB, nationality) collected at this phase is treated as high-sensitivity PII.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — personal data of third parties (directors and UBOs) who are not the applicant. Collected under MLR 2017 legal obligation (Article 6(1)(c) UK GDPR). Consent of the third parties is not the lawful basis — legal obligation is.
data_classification.retention: 5 years post-relationship end per MLR 2017 Regulation 40.
data_classification.transparency_note: Directors and UBOs are informed via the verification invitation email that their personal data will be processed for AML/CDD purposes under MLR 2017. Privacy notice link included in invitation.

regulatory_sla.obligation: MLR 2017 Regulation 28(3)(a) — identify and take reasonable measures to verify beneficial owners. No specific time limit; must be complete before account opening.

latency.notes: Per-individual identity verification latency mirrors JRN-001 PH-002 (Onfido/Jumio biometric + document check: 2–5 seconds vendor SLA). However, the total elapsed time for BPH-004 is measured in business days (not seconds) because multiple individuals must each independently complete their verification asynchronously. System latency per verification event is the same as JRN-001 PH-002; the phase SLA is 1–3 business days for all verifications to complete.

phase_completion_sla.notes: Each director/UBO receives an email invitation. If not completed within 48 hours, an automated reminder is sent. If not completed within 5 business days, the RM is escalated. The phase cannot close until all required verifications are complete.

concurrent_verifications.notes: A business with up to 10 directors/UBOs must be supportable. Each individual verification is an independent Onfido/Jumio session. SVC-050 must support concurrent sessions per application_id.

availability.degraded_mode: If Onfido/Jumio is unavailable, verification sessions are queued. Individuals can retry when the vendor recovers — their session link remains valid for 7 days.
availability.vendor_sla: Onfido/Jumio contractual SLA: 99.9% availability. Vendor degradation must not prevent new session initiation for more than 30 minutes.

nfr.security_notes: Each director/UBO verification session uses a vendor-issued JWT session token (time-limited, one-time use). Session tokens expire after 7 days. The applicant (PER-002) cannot complete another person's verification — the session token is bound to the invitation email address. Biometric data is not stored by the bank — outcome only (UK GDPR Article 9).

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGHEST — biometric processing (UK GDPR special category Article 9). DPIA covers extension of eKYC pipeline to business customer directors and UBOs.
data_classification.data_residency: UK only. Onfido/Jumio data processing must be within UK or adequacy-decision jurisdiction.

regulatory_sla.obligation: MLR 2017 Regulation 28(3) — verify identity of directors and UBOs using reliable and independent sources. No specific clock starts until all verifications are received. The 3–5 business day overall application SLA presupposes verifications complete within 2 business days.

latency.notes: Company-level and individual-level CDD runs in parallel across all directors and UBOs. Sanctions screening (SVC-051) must return within 3,000ms per individual (hard limit — GOV-005-R02). PEP and adverse media screening via ComplyAdvantage runs asynchronously with a 5–10 second typical latency. The BusinessKycAssessment aggregates all individual results — completion time is dominated by the slowest individual screening result.

nfr.sanctions_screening_notes: Hard regulatory limit. OFSI obligation requires real-time screening. Must screen company, all directors, and all UBOs against all applicable lists (OFSI, OFAC, UN, EU). If any individual screening call exceeds 3,000ms, SVC-051 must return an error and the screening must be retried. A breach of the 3,000ms hard limit must be logged to SVC-111 and treated as an operational incident.

edd_path_sla.notes: From the point EDD is triggered (BusinessKYCReferralRaised), the MLRO must be assigned within 4 hours. Total EDD completion SLA is 10 business days from application date. The RM has 5 business days to gather EDD documentation; the MLRO has 3 business days to review and decide.

throughput.notes: CDD screening for all individuals in an application runs in parallel. SVC-014 must support fan-out screening — a single application may trigger up to 10 parallel SVC-051 calls.

availability.degraded_mode: SVC-051 is a hard dependency (sanctions screening must complete before CDD can clear). If SVC-051 is unavailable, KYC clearance is withheld until screening can complete. Applications are queued; PER-002 is not informed of the reason for delay.
availability.planned_maintenance_window: No planned maintenance permitted during UK business hours. 02:00–04:00 UTC weekday only (minimum impact window).

nfr.security_notes: No customer interaction in this phase. All service-to-service calls use mTLS. CDD results are classified HIGHEST sensitivity (GOV-005-R01). Access restricted to SVC-014, MLRO (PER-052) via case management. Tipping-off prohibition (POCA 2002 s333A) is a functional requirement — no CDD data must be surfaced to the customer in any error message or UI state.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGHEST — regulatory AML data. Not surfaced to PER-002. Access restricted to SVC-014 and MLRO.
data_classification.retention: 5 years per MLR 2017 Regulation 40. WORM audit pipeline (SVC-111).

regulatory_sla.obligation: MLR 2017 Regulation 33 — EDD must be completed before establishing a business relationship where EDD conditions are met. OFSI Consolidated List screening must occur in real time (GOV-005-R02). SAR submission to NCA within 5 business days of forming a suspicion if applicable (GOV-005-R01).

latency.notes: Automated decision engine in SVC-005. Decision logic is rule-based (no ML inference latency). Decision must be synchronous within the request handling the BusinessKYCCleared event.

manual_referral_sla.notes: Referred applications require RM recommendation within 2 business days. If no action by day 3, escalation to Head of Commercial Banking.

availability.notes: Decision engine failure results in application hold — not a visible error to PER-002. Applications are retried automatically when the service recovers.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — decision outcome is a regulatory record (Consumer Duty evidence).
data_classification.retention: 7 years (decision record — BCOBS/Consumer Duty equivalent for business banking).

regulatory_sla.obligation: BBRS: decline acknowledgements must be sent within 5 working days. Complaint-handling SLA applies from receipt of complaint about a decision (GOV-002-R03).

latency.notes: BusinessAccount entity creation, account number/sort code allocation from the commercial banking range, multi-signatory configuration write, and BusinessAccountOpened/BusinessAccountProvisioned event publication. Slightly higher latency than personal account provisioning (JRN-001 PH-005) due to multi-signatory configuration setup.

idempotency.notes: Account provisioning must be idempotent — duplicate BusinessAccountOpened events must not result in duplicate accounts. Idempotency key: application_id.

availability.notes: Account provisioning is the highest-criticality phase. A failure here creates an approved-but-unprovisioned application that requires manual recovery. 99.99% target reflects this.
availability.degraded_mode: Auto-retry on failure. After 3 retries, PER-060 (IT Operations) is alerted. PER-002 is informed of delay.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — financial account data. FSCS SCV update where applicable.
data_classification.retention: Duration of account relationship + 7 years post-closure.

regulatory_sla.obligation: CASS business account registration — where business CASS regime is extended (GOV-002-R06), registration must occur within 7 days of account opening.

latency.notes: Credential creation and FIDO2/WebAuthn device registration via SVC-100. Business portal initialisation (role-based access configuration, account data fetch from SVC-005). Similar to JRN-001 PH-006.

availability.notes: Slight relaxation vs provisioning — account is already live; digital channel activation failure does not prevent the customer from telephoning to access their account. PER-002 can retry later.
availability.degraded_mode: If SVC-100 (IAM) is unavailable, digital channel activation is queued. Business account is provisioned and active; digital access follows when SVC-100 recovers.

nfr.security_notes: PSR 2017 Regulation 100 SCA compliance. FIDO2/WebAuthn device binding for each authorised user. Each user's credential is bound to their registered email address from the business application.

data_classification.sensitivity: HIGH — authentication credentials and biometric SCA enrolment (FIDO2 — biometric template stays on device).
data_classification.retention: Credential records retained for duration of user's authorised access + 7 years.

regulatory_sla.obligation: No specific regulatory SLA for digital channel activation itself. PSR 2017 SCA obligations apply to all authenticated access from activation onwards.

breakdown.BPH-005: Same day as last verification (automated CDD screening, target <30 minutes)
breakdown.BPH-006_to_BPH-008: Same day as CDD clearance (automated decisioning and provisioning)

breakdown.EDD_review: Up to 7 business days (MLRO review, document gathering)
